segments: 532 Chronography of Barhebraeus.
to Sir Henry,
the father of the lord of Cyprus,
an old and intelligent man;
and to him they entrusted the management of the youth and the administration of the kingdom.
And at that time,
two brothers, the sons of Sheikh Adi,
whom the Kurds of the region of Mosul held as a prophet, became hostile to each other.
And because one of them took a wife from the Mongols,
the other one became afraid,
and took all his people, about four hundred souls,
and fled to Syria, along with all the sheep, cattle, and horses that they possessed.
For the Christians were greatly terrified,
and feared him, lest on his passage he plunder and kill them.
He, however, passed by without harming anyone.
Nevertheless, after he had gone,
certain robbers came and invaded the village of Beth Takshur in the region of Nineveh.
And the shaven-headed {villagers} resisted them in battle,
and killed about ten of the robbers.
And of the villagers, five men were killed,
and seven young women and three boys were abducted.
And when the year 1587 [AD 1275/6] began,
it was:
On Thursday, the third of Tishrin I, there was a violent earthquake in the city of Arkestia, which is Arjish;
and its strong walls and all its buildings fell down,
and the majority of its inhabitants perished.
Likewise, in the city of Khilat and in its region that same earthquake occurred at the ninth hour,
and destruction took place in it,
though not total like that which occurred in Arjish.
And in those days, when a great caravan of Christian merchants was setting out from Cilicia for the territory of the Romans,
three hundred Turkmen horsemen fell upon them,
and killed about eighty merchants from among the notables of the Christians, near the city of Heraclea;
and they carried off the provisions and goods that were with them.
With one single merchant from the family of Isa bar Hasiri,
there were one hundred and twenty thousand Tyrian dinars.
And nothing escaped from that caravan,
except for four Arab camels.
And in the winter of that year,
Mongol armies gathered, about seventy thousand,
and marched against the fortress of Birah to capture it,
but they were not able to prevail,
by reason of the heavy snow that fell,
and the severe cold that came.
